headline: New Robotic Mastectomy Offers Less-Invasive Breast Cancer Treatment
meta_description: Oakland's Alta Bates Summit Medical Center introduces newly cleared robotic surgery that preserves natural appearance for breast cancer patients.
summary_short: A groundbreaking robotic mastectomy technique, now available at an East Bay hospital, offers patients a less-invasive option that preserves breast appearance.
body:
Oakland's Alta Bates Summit Medical Center is bringing a newly cleared robotic mastectomy technique to the Bay Area, offering breast cancer patients a less-invasive surgical option that preserves the natural look and feel of the breast.

Vicky Pan, 46, of Moraga, became one of the first patients in the region to undergo the procedure. The innovative approach represents a significant advancement in surgical precision, allowing surgeons to remove cancerous tissue while maintaining the patient's appearance and body image—a crucial consideration for many facing this diagnosis.

The introduction of this technology at a major East Bay medical center expands treatment options for cancer patients in the region, demonstrating how advancing surgical innovation can deliver both medical effectiveness and improved quality of life.
quick_facts: New robotic mastectomy technique now available at Alta Bates Summit Medical Center in Oakland
Surgery preserves the natural look and feel of the breast
Patient Vicky Pan, 46, from Moraga, among first to undergo procedure
Less-invasive option for breast cancer treatment in the Bay Area
